discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulating states and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: formerly University of Texas at Austin; now in Israel

subfield: Condensed matter physics (moire materials, strongly correlated electrons, superconductivity)
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands almost perfectly flat, so interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and coworkers realised this precisely, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that can be switched by a gate voltage. This was a theoretical prediction confirmed experimentally, and many groups and platforms have since reproduced and extended it: twisted multilayers, transition-metal dichalcogenides, orbital magnetism and fractional Chern insulators. The discovery created moire quantum matter as a new field. It provides a tunable laboratory for strong correlations, band topology and quantum geometry, which explains how superconductivity can survive in flat bands with vanishing band velocity. Few recent discoveries have reshaped condensed matter physics so profoundly or united theory and experiment so clearly.
